title: Elastic TPU/Graphene Microneedle-Mesh Interfaces via Microfluidic Patterning for Electrophysiology in Neural Organoids (Published)
abstract: Connecting electronics to neural organoids is key for brain-machine interfaces and studying neural systems, but 3D tissue surfaces make electrophysiology difficult. We present a stretchable mesh electrode array with graphene microneedles, made via microfluidic patterning for low-cost, reproducible fabrication. The device's microneedles and liquid metal-polymer interconnects withstand 200% strain, improving electrode-tissue contact and enabling robust multisite recordings. Over 60% of channels were activated, outperforming standard 2D electrodes. This biocompatible interface addresses mechanical mismatch issues, advancing studies of neural networks in 3D models.

title: Organoid Vascularization through Perfusion Vessel Model utilizing mesh-MPC Scaffold (Failed)
abstract: This project represents a purposeful and significant initiative dedicated to developing a perfusion vessel model for organoid vascularization. My responsibilities included assisting in the fabrication and characterization of the mesh-MPC scaffold, which plays a critical role in both supporting endothelial cell seeding and providing spatial cues for capillary neovascularization. Despite the project's ultimate fail, the absence of observable capillary networks surrounding the artificial vessel, with the underlying causes remaining undetermined—this experience has substantially deepened my comprehension of tissue engineering principles and the intricate dynamics inherent to organoid development.

title: Three-dimensional Liquid Metal-based Neuro-interfaces for Human Hippocampal Organoids
abstract: It was an invaluable experience to involved in a newly accepted top-tier journal, through which I gained experimental proficiency and started my research journey. Throughout this process, I have mastered the principles and protocols underlying the fabrication of metal-polymer conductors via microfluidic patterning based on polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Concurrently, I have attained proficiency in the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) system, encompassing both its hardware configuration and software operation. Furthermore, I have acquired a diverse array of research-relevant skills, for which I am deeply indebted to Postdoctoral Researcher Wu Yan.
